package_info.package_manager: PyPI (and other platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker)
package_info.package_versions: Not specified; applies to all versions where tunnel client is available
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers abuse the legitimate Cloudflare Tunnel client by installing and executing it on compromised systems to establish persistent, outbound-only, encrypted tunnels. This enables covert remote access and data exfiltration while bypassing traditional network defenses, such as inbound firewall rules and network monitoring, making detection and remediation significantly more difficult.

execution_context.file_location: Victim system shell or command line interface after Cloudflare Tunnel client installation
required_permissions: filesystem (to install and execute the client)
process execution (to launch the tunnel process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker executes a shell command to launch the Cloudflare Tunnel client with a unique token, which initiates an outbound-only, encrypted tunnel from the victim's machine to attacker-controlled Cloudflare infrastructure, enabling persistent remote access and covert data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This command establishes a persistent, encrypted communication channel from the victim system to external Cloudflare infrastructure, bypassing inbound firewall restrictions and enabling the attacker to remotely access and control the compromised host without detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: While Cloudflare Tunnels are intended for authorized users to securely expose internal services, in this context, the tunnel is deployed by an attacker to provide unauthorized, stealthy access and facilitate data theft from a compromised system.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DevOps and IT teams may use Cloudflare Tunnels for secure, authorized remote access to internal applications or services as part of normal business operations.
key_indicators: Installation and execution of cloudflared or similar tunnel clients outside of approved IT workflows
Use of unique tunnel tokens not registered with legitimate IT operations or asset management
Persistent outbound-only network connections to Cloudflare-controlled endpoints
On-demand appearance of cloudflared processes correlating with attacker activity
Presence of cloudflared binary or installer in unexpected locations on endpoints

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains initial access to the victim system through methods such as malware infection, phishing, or supply chain compromise.
Cloudflare Tunnel client is installed on the victim system, either manually by the attacker or via automated tooling.
Attacker executes the tunnel creation command with a unique token, establishing a covert, outbound-only tunnel to Cloudflare infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy remote access and data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages the established tunnel for persistent, stealthy access and to exfiltrate sensitive data from the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attack completion, including data theft or further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Installation and execution of cloudflared or similar tunnel clients outside of approved change windows or IT workflows
Persistent outbound-only connections to Cloudflare infrastructure from endpoints not authorized for such activity
On-demand activation of cloudflared tunnel processes that appear only during periods of attacker activity
Unusual process execution patterns involving cloudflared with tunnel tokens not associated with legitimate business operations
file_indicators: Presence of cloudflared binary or installer on endpoints, especially in non-standard directories
Unusual process execution of cloudflared with tunnel tokens not registered with IT asset management
Cloudflared configuration files or logs in unexpected locations
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains matching *.cloudflare.com or specific Cloudflare tunnel endpoints
DNS queries for tunnel-specific hostnames associated with Cloudflare Tunnels
Sustained encrypted outbound traffic to Cloudflare IP ranges from endpoints not typically using such services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation and execution of Cloudflare Tunnel clients (e.g., cloudflared) on endpoints, especially outside of authorized IT workflows. Correlate process creation events for cloudflared with outbound network connections to Cloudflare infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries or network traffic to tunnel-specific hostnames or IPs not associated with legitimate business use. Maintain and regularly update a list of approved tunnel tokens and endpoints; flag any unauthorized usage or new tokens. Investigate the presence of cloudflared binaries, configuration files, or logs in non-standard locations, and review process execution patterns for signs of on-demand tunnel activation.
